subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack setup/docs explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments to address the remaining latency gap, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond guidance?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured gap is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but stronger guidance or defaults affect setup expectations and deployment requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and add explicit latency guidance that hosted public-ingress Slack deployments should prefer HTTP Request URLs.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger Slack setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the existing transport table is sufficient and close this later with a recorded no-change product decision.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and add explicit latency guidance that hosted public-ingress Slack deployments should prefer HTTP Request URLs.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurements and merged the partial current-main fix, and they scoped the remaining work to HTTP mode guidance.
